utterances.text: There have been several meetings with the Professor Duma and with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall any particular meeting, perhaps in the month of November of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I don't remember the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall perhaps that some of those meetings took place in the year 2001, between August of 2001 and the end of the year?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been meetings discussing when the autopsy should -- that is, the exhumation, when it should start, regarding the present preparations and people were discussing our security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall whether those meetings were in the year 2001 still or is that too far gone, that you can't recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. If I can ask to you look back at the document in front of you, there's another paragraph which says this: "During the meeting, representatives of the ICTY were clearly and precisely explained the ICTY's authorisations in regard of the procedure, enforcement, and its consequences over our state, these which would accrue as a result of the impossibility to continue the Court procedure in relation to the Ljuboten event." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's another paragraph which was read to you by my colleague yesterday, which says this: "In this context we would like to mention that this is our first serious and official conversation regarding the critical incidents with both representative of the Macedonian judiciary and the international community. During our talks with representative of the ICTY, they were categorical," and then we go on to the next page, "that it is it of essential need to respect the basic postulates for professionalism and criteria for good professional work." Sir, are you able to say what meeting Professor Duma was referring to in this particular part of his report?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the meeting that took place, that is being discussed in the letter in the first paragraph, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you recall the date of that meeting, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is listed. Maybe you can bring back the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can bring back the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that the meeting of the 30th of January, sir, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether this refers to that particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we can --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it refers to the meeting held at the institute with the president of the court and the officials from the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one such meeting, in any case, took place in January 2002, but you cannot tell whether there had been any similar meeting prior to that time. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been meetings, but the director is the one present at all meetings and some professors from the institute, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to the second page of the document now. It is the end of the first -- of the previous paragraph, the paragraph from the previous page which Professor Duma makes a point about the financial independence of the institute. But then I would like to ask you to focus on the last paragraph of that document. And I read it out to you. It says: "Beside this situation, professional staff of the Forensic Institute reckoned that further delay of the commencement of the activities of ICTY in analysing the concrete event might have negative repercussions over the Macedonian state, and therefore it was decided to provide the requested documentation to the authorised court in hope that the authorised institutions and body of the state will provide conditions for further work and existence of the institute in all its segments." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall Professor Duma complaining to you about the unwillingness of the Office of the Prosecution to act very fast or to be proactive in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can this witness please be shown N000-9883-30. And the Macedonian version of this document is N000-9911-MY. Your Honour, this is a letter which was lifted out of a larger Prosecution exhibit. That's Rule 65 ter number 20, and the Macedonian version of this document appears to be a translation of the English, which itself would be a translation of a document which we don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have copies, Your Honour, because we hadn't had time to place it in the binder. If the usher may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps if the usher to give a copy to the Prosecutor -- oh, they have it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir,, if I may ask you to look at the top left-hand corner of that document. It says: "Public prosecution of the Republic of Macedonia," then there's a number 11/2002 and a date 14 August 2002. And the letter is addressed to ICTY OTP Madam Carla Del Ponte. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the subject of that letter is a response to the request for information submitted by the Prosecutor of ICTY. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the first sentence immediately below, it says: "The public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia has the pleasure and honour to respond to the request for information submitted on 5 August 2002." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I may ask the registry to turn to the -- what is the third page of that document with number 4 at the bottom of the page. It is N000-09914.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you, sir, to find a paragraph starting with the word "the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal," and there's a date 26/04/2002. I believe it is page 31 of the Macedonian, at the bottom of the page has a 31. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I opened the page 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a paragraph which says that "The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal, in the same letter, dated 26 April 2002, has indeed informed the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia that the international Tribunal, according to Article 9 of the statute of the court, has primacy over the national courts of the Republic of Macedonia and informed the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia that they would be involved in the already-commenced investigations in relation to the crimes committed in the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say that, "However, information has not arrived to the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, whether the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal acted in accordance with Article 9 of the rules of procedure and evidence of the International Criminal Tribunal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at the bottom of this same page in the English, in any case, it says, "In the past period the formal official deferral request has not been delivered by the International Tribunal to the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia or the court," and that is the next page in the English, please, "in accordance with Article 10 of the rules of procedure and evidence of the International Tribunal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if you jump over the text of that provision and go to what is noted down as paragraph 4 it says: "The public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia was not informed with any letter or decision of The Hague Tribunal that the Macedonian authorities should cease all further investigations in relation to these cases. And as a result of that in the Republic of Macedonia, in accordance with the constitution, the law on criminal procedure, criminal code and other laws, acts have been undertaken by the competent organs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "These acts have been undertaken in relation to the known and unknown perpetrators which are revealed additionally during the proceedings." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the person who signed this document, we will see it is Prosecutor Dzikov, says: "Reference the cooperation between the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, his/her office and the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, both parties emphasised many times that it was on a more than a satisfactory level." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Dzikov says this: "Meetings have been held many times in order to assist OTP of The Hague Tribunal in Skopje in relation to the pending obstacles which they have in relation to the investigation they conduct and adequate results have been achieved after those meetings." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then Prosecutor Dzikov says: "In the meeting held on 8 May 2002 in Skopje between the chief Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal and the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, it was agreed to form an expert team consisted of six experts who, in the Republic of Macdonia, would contact adequate team to work in relation to the investigations for which the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal was interested, but to this date we were not informed about forming such a team." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at the very bottom of that page there's a comment which starts on the last line which says: "The public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia," and I will ask the registry to turn to the next page in the English, please. "The public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia informs you that up to date most correctly and most consciously has forwarded all relevant information in its possession to the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is signed by public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia Stavre Dzikov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would wish to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D75, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, there is another letter which I would like to show to you, and it is N000-9883-39 in the English, N000-9883-42 in the Macedonian, and in the usher's assistance, we have hard copies for the Court, the Prosecution and the witness. Thank you. Sir, do you have that letter in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Again at the first page on the top left-hand corner. It says that it is the Republic of Macedonia, public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Macedonia, same number as the previous letter, 11 -- seems to be that same number. Yes, same number as the previous letter, 11/2002. This letter is dated 2nd September 2002. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sent to the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia, Office of the Prosecutor, Madam Carla Del Ponte. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you could turn quickly to the last page of that document, in Macedonian or in English. Would you agree that the document is again signed by public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, Stavre Dzikov?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the document has a heading saying -- there's a reference and then there's a subject respond to a letter. It's addressed to Madam Del Ponte, and Mr. Dzikov says the following: "Please allow me to address you by this letter regarding the different legal opinions and views on the interpretation of the primacy provisions of the Tribunal over the national judiciary of Republic of Macedonia between the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY and public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could turn to the next page after that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, there's a paragraph started with the word "as I already clearly and precisely informed." Can you find it on the second or third page of the Macedonian document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you. It says: "As I already clearly and precisely informed you in my previous letter, it is essential to follow the formal procedures for deferral of the cases which are conducted in our courts by ICTY submitting an official request for deferral of the competence to our courts which are conducting the cases through the supreme court of Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dzikov goes on to say: "So far in our successful and fruitful mutual cooperation, an agreement for exchange of relevant information was achieved in relation to the cases that are you interested in in accordance with Rule 8 of the Rules." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if we can turn to the third page in the English. I believe that would in part also on the third page in the Macedonian. Mr. Dzikov says this: "Our communication was established on the basis of actual cooperation, direct meetings and statement of the Prosecutors on the basis of Article 8 of the rules of procedure and evidence, where only relevant information are sought. Then Prosecutor Dzikov says this: "The security situation in Republic of Macedonia, even after 26 September 2002, is still endangered by constant attacks of person that use violence for political goals." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he goes on to say that "There are still murders of civilian persons and members of the security forces, kidnapping of civilian persons, violent acts from the Albanian terrorist gangs, which call themselves army of Republic [indiscernible] and ANA, Albanian Liberation Army, and terrorist gangs from the protectorate, Kosovo." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the last paragraph of his letter to Madam Del Ponte Prosecutor Dzikov says this: "Because of this critical condition of the state, the postponing of the prosecution and the hesitancy of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY and the ICTY which lead to expansion of the terrorism and serious violations of the international humanitarian law and in order to reconcile the legal views regarding the exercising of primacy, I consider that there a need of an urgent joint working meeting with you and the president of the ICTY, Judge Jorda." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would wish to tender this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is one last document I would wish to show you and it's under tab 40 of your binder. It is Prosecution document Rule 65 ter 61, ERN N000-4211-ET-01. And the Macedonian version is N000-4211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see, Mr. Mettraux, at line 11 that the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Would the registrar repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The previous document will become Exhibit 1D76, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir that in April of 2002 when the bodies from Ljuboten were exhumed, your institute also carried out an examination of the clothing of the deceased; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again this was done upon the request of the investigative judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as this document would suggest, the results of those examinations were then sent back to the investigative judge of the Lower Court Skopje II. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this particular document which is in front of you was signed by you, by Dr. Cakar and by the director Aleksej Duma. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we wish to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D77, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, my attention is drawn to the fact that document under tab 38 of the binder, which is a section protocol relating to unknown person number 1, that's Rami Jusufi, which I've shown to the witness, I haven't formally sought to tender it and I would wish to do so with the Court's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski, is there anything left?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I will be short. I hold the witness for a short time only because only a few topics have remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Zlatko Jakovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I am Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic we appear on behalf of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Today I will make you some questions which I think my learned colleague Mr. Mettraux did not tackle. You said you had participated in the exhumation of the bodies in Ljuboten on April the 2nd, where an investigating judge had participated, representatives of the ICTY, deputy public prosecutor. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the exhumation the bodies were put in a bag which was sealed by the representatives of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the bag with a corpse was put --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: A tin, which was then sealed?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then the tin was put -- was sent to the Forensic Institute and was put in the refrigerator, which was sealed by representatives of the Tribunal. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, from the time of the exhumation until it -- its putting in the refrigerator of the Forensic Institute, none of the persons with the exception of those present at the exhumation could not have had access to the corpse. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the refrigerator, the tin was sent to the autopsy room where the autopsy was conducted. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: During the autopsy, there were representatives from the criminalistic technique department, an investigating judge and representatives of the Tribunal. Is this correct.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you participated to all -- to the autopsies of all the corpses brought from the exhumation of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally conducted three of them and I participated to the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To my colleague Mr. Mettraux you answered that in the clothes of one of the corpses 26 bullets from a gun-fire were found. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the inspection of the clothes of another corpse, a wallet with money was found, with documents, ID, and a driving licence. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You said that your institute works also upon the order of investigating judge pursuant of the procedural -- I'm sorry, the law on criminal procedure. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can the investigating judge issue an order for a paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this order is issued because an expertise is needed while conducting an investigating procedure as evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, I speak of the period in 2001/2002 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 2000/2001.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation is not correct. 2000/2001 is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. My question referred to 2000/2001. Is it correct that in that period of time the investigating judges in the Republic of Macedonia accepted the paraffin glove test as an evidence for use of fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time and now as well they accepted as an evidence proving the usage of fire-arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the statement 65 ter 2D00-178.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a statement made by Ognen Stavrev. On the first page, it can be seen that while making the statement Mr. Ognen Stavrev was a criminal judge and his previous profession was an investigating judge. You said you knew Mr. Ognen Stavrev. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On page 2, please could you turn to page 2 of the statement. Paragraph 2, the Judge Ognen Stavrev says that he became investigating judge by the end of 1999 or beginning of 2000. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 3 of the English version and page 4 of the Macedonian version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In his statement the Judge Ognen Stavrev, in paragraph 10 says: "In general, all the accused said that they were hiding in the basements because they were afraid of the shooting. However, the positive results of their paraffin tests was proof that they had been handling weapons. What accused ever said that he is guilty? On the basis of the paraffin glove test, I, being an investigative judge, thought that the accused might have committed a crime. For me, the gun powder test was enough." Is it correct that the investigative Judge Ognen Stavrev considered that the positive paraffin glove test is enough of an evidence that a person handled a fire, a gun?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to his statement that you have cited, the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Honourable Judges, I do not have any more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, earlier today you were asked about trajectory of a projectile in one of the bodies that you actually performed an autopsy on that had been exhumed in 2002. And with respect to that projectile you indicated that it travelled in the body upwards, from a downwards position up. And from that you testified that that travel or that trajectory would indicate the person who shot -- who was shot into the body was in a lower position in relation to the person who was the subject of the autopsy. My question to you is: Can you please tell us, by lower position, could this mean that the shooter was in a crouching position or perhaps lying down at the time that the projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the difference in height of four centimetres between the bone, that is to say, the left inguinal bone, and the left side of the body, this is just four centimetres, at a very short distance. I can say that the projectile entered the body under a sharp angle of around 50 to 60 degrees with respect to the vertical plane of the body, which points to the fact that if the person who is shooting at him, if the person was crouching or lying down, the person would be very close to the deceased. When I say close, I'm just talking about a metre or two. Or, the deceased might have been at a larger distance from the shooter, but maybe he was on a tree or a terrace, elevated position, and the shooter might have been lower.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And if we could refer back to your testimony from yesterday, it's actually page 45 of yesterday' transcript. You were asked about requests for autopsies from the city hospital. Are you asked to do an autopsy for every death that occurs at this particular hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this hospital and other hospitals throughout the Republic of Macedonia, we receive requests to conduct an autopsy of individuals who have died of a violent death, persons where the diagnosis is missing, for persons who died during a surgery or any other type of medical intervention, as well as persons who died during the initial 24 hours after they have been admitted to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And on page 46 of the transcript from yesterday, you were also shown a document that has already been admitted as P00054.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please display that once again. It is actually tab 14 of the binder provided by the Defence for Mr. Boskoski. And for further assistance, it was -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, do you recall this note being shown to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in this Official Note, it is signed by the investigating judge Velce Pancevski at the very bottom. And just to refresh your memory a little bit, at the very top of the note under the words Official Note, it indicates that on 14 August 2001, I, being the investigative judge, visited the city general hospital in Skopje and talked with Dr. Viktor Kamilovski with regard to the health condition of the following detained individuals, and then it lists Nevaip Bajrami, Ismail Ramadani, Adem Ametovski, and then fourth is Qaili Atulla. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please display for the witness the witness statement of Velce Pancevski, which is at ERN N002-2031, N002-2037, Macedonian translation being the same with a MF at the end. Doctor, do you see here a Macedonian version of this particular witness statement. It's from Velce Pancevski, and at that time his current occupation was investigative judge in Basic Court II in Skopje. And then the date of the interview with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor was on 14 and 19 December 2005. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to page 4 of the English version of this particular statement, which is page 5 of the Macedonian. If I could draw your attention to paragraph 12. It indicates that the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor have shown me, that is being investigative judge Pancevski, a document bearing the ERN N001-9824. This document, he indicates, is a copy of my internal notes that I made about some of the accused who were seriously injured. This is my handwriting. This is just my internal note. It is not official evidence and it is not a part of the records. At the bottom here it says: "This is just my," if we could turn the page in English, please. It says that: "This is just my reminder and was photocopied without my knowledge and approval. "In response to the question whether the indication of serious injuries in my notes could indicate that some of the accused were victims of crimes rather than perpetrators of crimes, I say that I cannot answer that question, because in this case we were dealing with accused and not victims." Do you see that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could please then show exhibit -- that is a -- an exhibit that has already been admitted under P54. It is located at pages 182 and 183 of e-court. However, for purposes of the English translation, it might be better to pull 65 ter 19.8 which has a corresponding English translation. Actually, the Macedonian version that was on the screen earlier was correct. And I believe the English translation can be found at 65 ter 19.58. Thank you very much. Doctor, I'm now showing you a document that bears the same ERN that investigative judge Pancevski referred to in paragraph 12 of his statement that we just went over. The document bears ET N001-9824-N001-9825. At the very top of this document it is dated 14 August 2001. I believe there is a time there in parentheses, 2320, and goes on to indicate general city hospital, Skopje, it lists the Dr. Kamilovski, Viktor. And goes on further. Down below that it says Atulla Qaili, deceased, and then it lists three other names and then it goes on at number one it says Bajrami Nevaip and then at number -- right below that, I'm sorry, it says diagnosis, heads -- head -- there's something illegible, head, ribs fracture, 7, 8, 9 left thoracic cage, and then at number 2 it says Ramadani Ismail. It indicates a received date and a time, and then it says diagnosis, pains in head and thoracic cage, head contusion, ribs fracture, 7th and 8th right and 2nd to 7th rib, left side, haematoma, right eye. At number 3 it lists Ametovski, Adem. It indicates a diagnosis 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, ribs fracture, brain concussion, left side, face, and there is something illegible, scratches. And then at the bottom there it says haematoma, left eye. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn the page in both versions, please. And at number 4, the investigative judge, in his handwriting he writes Qaili Atulla, and then at the bottom it says received 13/8/2001, 0500, in unconsciousness condition, head contusion, arm, something illegible, face below his left eye, neck contusion, contusion, whole body with haematomas. Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And are these particular injuries, the ones listed for Qaili Atulla, consistent with some of the injuries that you noted during the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: From looking at these handwriting notes by the investigative judge Pancevski and the Official Note that I just showed you that was prepared by the same judge, can you see that the information in these handwritten notes are not reflected in the Official Notes that were shown to you, which is Exhibit P00054?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the same details as they are here handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could we just please display P00054 so that the doctor could see the Official Note I'm referring to. And, again, Doctor, this is tab 14 of your binder that's before you. And, Doctor, I see that have you had an opportunity to look at the Macedonian version in hard copy. You indicated that the injuries were not in the same details as they are in the handwritten notes. Do you see any references to any of the injuries that were noted in the handwritten notes in this Official Note prepared by the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see only that it reads that they have been injured, medical assistance was provided and they're going to be kept for several days. Today they're not capable of communicating and giving their statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question for you, Doctor was in reference to yesterday's testimony at page 73 of the transcript you were asked about the paraffin glove test. Can I ask you, relying on your expertise regarding this particular test, can you tell me whether-- if someone was hit on the hands by a fire-arm, would that also leave nitrate particles that would be detected by this particular paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is very hypothetical. First of all, it all depends which part of a weapon would be used in order to hit a person. The location where the hit would occur, and from the theoretical point of view, one cannot exclude this from happening, bearing in mind that the powder particles would be found only at the particular location where the hit took place. And, at that particular location, there should be some kind of additional injury, like a bruise, contusion or excoriation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Motoike. Doctor, you will, I'm sure, be pleased to learn that that concludes the questioning of you in respect of this matter. The Chamber is very grateful for your attendance here in The Hague, for the patience and care with which you have given your assistance to the matters that have been put to you. We thank you for that and you are of course now able to return to your ordinary life and work. The court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I thank the Honourable Court as well.
